acceptanceCriteria: `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md` exists with a priority table whose rows carry a threat id, priority, threat, mitigating invariant, and the requirement IDs that hold the invariant.
A generator produces `docs/threats.json` from the table and a `threats-check` GATE_STEPS entry fails on drift, with a `_test.sh` neighbour like `script/check-decision-numbers_test.sh`.
Every requirement ID cited in the table resolves in `docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv`.
body:
Filed on 2026-09-22 from a review of https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate (head d277088, 2026-09-22).

Corvint has no threat model document. Only four specs mention threats in passing (`docs/specs/test-claim-qualification-v0.md`, `docs/specs/mcp-test-validity-profile-v0.md`, `docs/specs/local-observability-dashboard-v0.md`, decision 0320). The product invariants that are security-relevant (secret-screened learning, tainted sources never satisfying a basis in V1-0090, read commands never mutating, no network on the default path) are stated in AGENTS.md and scattered specs but never enumerated as threats with a named mitigating invariant and a priority.

Substrate keeps a prose threat model (`docs/threat-model.md`) whose priority table has one row per threat: id, priority, threat, mitigating invariant, suggested concrete mitigations, notes. `hack/export-threats.py` exports the table to `docs/threats.json` and `hack/verify/threats.sh` fails when the JSON drifts from the Markdown. The invariant column is the useful part: each row names a property that, if held, removes the threat, rather than a specific fix.

Proposal: add `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md` with that table shape for Corvint's own boundaries (local repository data as untrusted input, provider records, learned traces, host adapters, the optional console, the MCP surface), a generated `docs/threats.json`, and a `threats-check` step in GATE_STEPS next to `decision-numbers-check`. Each row should cite the spec requirement ID that carries its invariant so `docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv` and the registry cannot disagree silently. The JSON is the natural input for the security-review skill.
title: docs: machine-readable threat registry with a drift gate
